```{r, echo = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# Libraries
library(here) #set local working directory
library(tidyverse) #for data manipulation
library(emmeans) #for calculating estimated marginal means
library(multcomp) #for calculating CIs and tukey test
library(multcompView) #for labeling with letters
library(cowplot) #for joining plot panels
```

```{r include = FALSE}
# Import data
data <- read_csv(here("data", "VanScoyoc_et_al_data.csv"))
```

```{r}
# Center and standardize diurnal activity ratios
data <- data %>% 
        mutate(#center and standardize predator data
               pr_low_rescale = (pr_low_D_AR-0.5)*2 + #rescale diurnal activity from (0-1) to (-1-1)
                                 (-((pr_low_D_AR-0.5)*2)), #set low data to zero 
               pr_high_rescale = (pr_high_D_AR-0.5)*2 + #rescale diurnal activity from (0-1) to (-1-1)
                                 (-((pr_low_D_AR-0.5)*2)), #add opposite of pr_low_rescaled
               #center and standardize prey data
               py_low_rescale = (py_low_D_AR-0.5)*2 + #rescale diurnal activity from (0-1) to (-1-1)
                                 (-((py_low_D_AR-0.5)*2)), #set low data to zero 
               py_high_rescale = (py_high_D_AR-0.5)*2 + #rescale from (0-1) to (-1-1)
                                 (-((py_low_D_AR-0.5)*2))) #add opposite of pr_low_rescaled
```



```{r}
# Tidy data for Figure2a
fig2a_data <- data %>% #call dataset
                dplyr::select(pair_ID, #select columns
                              pr_low_rescale, pr_high_rescale, 
                              py_low_rescale, py_high_rescale) %>% 
                pivot_longer(2:5) %>% #pivot data to long format for tidying human_activity level
                separate(name,c("type","human_activity"), sep = "_") %>% #separate columns
                mutate(type = ifelse(type == "pr", "predator", "prey")) %>% 
                pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = value) #pivot wide for plotting
```

```{r}
# Fig 2a Plot

# Behavioral response pathway labels for plot 
plot_labels <- data.frame(name = c("Predator Attraction", "Mutual Attraction", 
                                   "Mutual Avoidance", "Prey Refuge"),
                          x = c(-0.75, 0.75, -0.75, 0.75), 
                          y = c(0.82, 0.82, -0.92, - 0.92))
                          
plot_colors <- factor(c("#D6AEF8","#EDF7B5","#EDF7B5","#D6AEF8"))

# Plot
fig2a <- ggplot() +
        #Add data
            geom_line(data = fig2a_data, aes(x=prey, y=predator, #add lines grouped by pair_id 
                                             group = pair_ID), color = "grey60") +
            geom_point(data = fig2a_data, aes(x=prey, y=predator), alpha = 0.7) + #add points   
            geom_label(data = plot_labels, aes(x = x, y = y, #add behavioral response pathway 
                                               label = name,
                                               fill = plot_colors,
                                               alpha = 0.2), 
                                    size = 3.2, family="serif") +
          #Format plot
            scale_fill_manual(values = c("#EDF7B5","#D6AEF8")) + #fill labels with theme colors
            guides(fill="none", alpha="none") + #remove fill legend
            labs(x = "", y = "") +
            #labs(x = "Prey (relative change in diurnal activity ratio)", 
            #     y = "Predator (relative change in diurnal activity ratio)") + #label axes
            geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype='dashed') + #set x-axis line
            geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype='dashed') + #set y-axis line
            lims(x=c(-1,1),y=c(-1,1)) + #set axis limits
            coord_fixed() + #fix plot dimensions
            theme_light() + #set theme
            theme(text=element_text(size=10, family="serif")) #set text size & font
fig2a
```

```{r}
# Figure 2a descriptive results

#Number of points per quadrant
fig2a_descriptive <- fig2a_data %>% #call dataset
    mutate(hypothesis = ifelse(predator < 0 & prey < 0, "Mutual Avoidance", 
                           ifelse(predator > 0 & prey > 0, "Mutual Attraction",
                             ifelse(predator > 0 & prey < 0, "Predator Attraction",
                                ifelse(predator < 0 & prey > 0, "Prey Refuge", 
                                       "Neutral"))))) %>% 
  filter(human_activity == "high") %>% 
  group_by(hypothesis) %>% 
  summarize(n = n()) %>% 
  mutate(percent = n/178*100)

fig2a_descriptive
```




```{r}
# Tidy data for Figure2b
fig2b_data <- data %>% #call dataset
                mutate(pr_shift_diurnal = pr_high_D_AR - pr_low_D_AR, #predator change in diurnality
                       py_shift_diurnal = py_high_D_AR - py_low_D_AR, #prey change in diurnality
                       hypothesis = ifelse(pr_shift_diurnal < 0 & py_shift_diurnal < 0, "Mutual Avoidance", 
                                  ifelse(pr_shift_diurnal > 0 & py_shift_diurnal > 0, "Mutual Attraction",
                                    ifelse(pr_shift_diurnal > 0 & py_shift_diurnal < 0, "Predator Attraction",
                                      ifelse(pr_shift_diurnal < 0 & py_shift_diurnal > 0, "Prey Refuge", 
                                             "Neutral"))))) %>% 
                dplyr::select(reference, pair_ID, #select columns for plotting
                              hypothesis, change_overlap) %>%
                filter(!grepl('Neutral', hypothesis)) %>% #remove neutral response dyads (n = 6)
                drop_na() #without dyads without overlap values (n = 5) 
  
#Results in 16 studies, n = 167 dyads
```

```{r}
# Calculate confidence intervalse for Figure 2b
model <- lm(change_overlap ~ hypothesis, data = fig2b_data) #set up model
model_means <- emmeans(object = model, specs = "hypothesis") #get adjusted weight means per group
model_means_cld <- cld(object = model_means, #add letters to each mean
                       adjust = "Tukey", Letters = letters, alpha = 0.05)
```

```{r}
# Figure 2b descriptive results

# Percent of predator or prey with increased overlap
fig2b_data %>% 
  mutate(direction_overlap = ifelse(change_overlap < 0, "decrease", 
                                ifelse(change_overlap > 0, "increase", "no_change"))) %>% 
  group_by(hypothesis, direction_overlap) %>% 
  summarize(n = n()) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction_overlap, values_from = n) %>% 
  mutate(total = sum(increase,decrease),
         perc_increase = increase/total*100,
         perc_decrease = decrease/total*100)
```



```{r}
# Behavioral response pathway labels for plot 
plot_labels2 <- data.frame(name = c("Prey Refuge", "Predator Attraction",
                                    "Mutual Avoidance", "Mutual Attraction"),
                           y = c(-0.27,-0.27,0.28, 0.28), 
                           x = c(1.3,2.3,3.3,4.3))

plot_colors2 <- factor(c("#D6AEF8","#D6AEF8","#EDF7B5","#EDF7B5"))

# Fig 2b Plot 

fig2b <- ggplot() +
      #Add data
          geom_point(data = fig2b_data, aes(y = change_overlap, x = fct_relevel(hypothesis, 
            "Prey Refuge","Predator Attraction","Mutual Avoidance","Mutual Attraction")), #add points
            shape = 16, alpha = 0.5, position = position_nudge(x = -0.2)) +
          geom_boxplot(data = fig2b_data, aes(y = change_overlap, x = hypothesis), #add boxplot
            width = 0.2, outlier.shape = NA, position = position_nudge(x = 0)) +
          geom_point(data = model_means_cld, #add mean
                     aes(y = emmean, x = hypothesis), size = 1, color = "maroon") +
          geom_errorbar(data = model_means_cld, #add confidence intervals
                        aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL, x = hypothesis),
                        width = 0.05, color = "maroon") +
          geom_label(data = plot_labels2, aes(x = x, y = y, #add behavioral response pathway 
                                               label = name, 
                                               fill = plot_colors2, 
                                               alpha = 0.2), 
                                    size = 3.2, family="serif") +
      #Format plot
          scale_fill_manual(values = c("#EDF7B5","#D6AEF8","#EDF7B5","#EDF7B5")) + #fill plot labels
          guides(fill="none", alpha="none") + #remove fill legend
          labs(x = "", y = "Change in Temporal Overlap") + #label axes
          geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") + #set x-axis line
          theme_light() + #set theme
          theme(text=element_text(size=10, family="serif"), #format axis text   
                axis.title.y=element_blank(), #remove x axis   
                axis.text.y=element_blank(), #remove x axis   
                axis.ticks.y=element_blank()) + #remove x axis    
          coord_flip() + #flip plot orientation
          ylim(c(-0.5, 0.5)) #fix plot size
```

```{r fig2, fig.height = 4, fig.width = 6.5, dpi = 300}
# Combine Figure 2 plots
figure2 <- plot_grid(fig2a, fig2b, label_size = 12, #combine plots
                    align = "h", axis = "b", nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(3,1.7), 
                    hjust = c(0, -0.04))
figure2
ggsave("figure2.png", figure2, height = 4, width = 6.5, units = "in", dpi = 600)
```

**Fig. 2.** *Human influence on predator-prey temporal activity and overlap based on review of camera trap studies between paired settings of low and high human use. (a) Humans altered diel activity in mammal predator-prey dyads via four major pathways: mutual attraction, mutual avoidance, prey refuge, and prey switching. Lines reflect the relative magnitude and direction of diel activity response toward nocturnality (-1) or diurnality (1) for each predator-prey dyad at paired settings of low and high human use (n = 178 predator-prey dyads, 19 studies). (b) Change in predator-prey temporal overlap between settings of low and high human use did not vary predictably with predator-prey activity responses (n = 167 predator-prey dyads, 16 studies). Similar predator-prey responses (i.e., prey refuge, prey switching) to humans did not result in increased overlap between dyads, likewise opposite predator-prey responses (i.e., mutual attraction, mutual avoidance) to humans did not result in decreased overlap between dyads as predicted. Black dots represent change in temporal overlap for each dyad. Red error bars represent estimated marginal means and  ± 95% confidence interval.*
